sanskrit: virūpa uvāca kāmakrodhau viddhi nau tvam āvābhyāṃ kārito bhavān sameti ca yad uktaṃ te samā lokās tavāsya ca
english: Virūpa said: Know us two to be Desire and Wrath; it was by us that you were made to act. And as for the equality of which you spoke, your worlds and his are indeed equal.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ dhārayate kiṃ cij jijñāsā tvatkṛte kṛtā kālo dharmas tathā mṛtyuḥ kāmakrodhau tathā yuvām
english: This brāhmaṇa holds nothing back from you; this testing was done for your sake. Time, Dharma, and Death, Desire and Wrath — such are you two.

sanskrit: sarvam anyonyanikaṣe nighṛṣṭaṃ paśyatas tava gaccha lokāñ jitān svena karmaṇā yatra vāñchasi
english: All has been rubbed together upon the touchstone of mutual proof, as you have seen. Go now to the worlds you have won by your own deeds, wherever you wish.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca jāpakānāṃ phalāvāptir mayā te saṃprakīrtitā gatiḥ sthānaṃ ca lokāś ca jāpakena yathā jitāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: I have fully proclaimed to you the attainment of fruit by the reciters — the course, the abode, and the worlds, and how they are won by the reciter.

sanskrit: prayāti saṃhitādhyāyī brahmāṇaṃ parameṣṭhinam atha vāgniṃ samāyāti sūryam āviśate 'pi vā
english: He who studies the saṃhitā goes forth to Brahmā the Supreme; or else he draws near to Agni, or enters into the Sun.

sanskrit: sa taijasena bhāvena yadi tatrāśnute ratim guṇāṃs teṣāṃ samādatte rāgeṇa pratimohitaḥ
english: If, through his fiery nature, he takes delight there, then, deluded by attachment, he assumes the qualities of those realms.

sanskrit: evaṃ some tathā vāyau bhūmyākāśaśarīragaḥ sarāgas tatra vasati guṇāṃs teṣāṃ samācaran
english: So too in Soma and in Vāyu; clothed in the body of earth and ether, still bound by attachment, he dwells there, partaking of their qualities.

sanskrit: atha tatra virāgī sa gacchati tv atha saṃśayam param avyayam icchan sa tam evāviśate punaḥ
english: But if there he becomes free of attachment, he passes beyond all uncertainty; longing for the supreme and imperishable, he enters into That alone once more.

sanskrit: amṛtāc cāmṛtaṃ prāptaḥ śītībhūto nirātmavān brahmabhūtaḥ sa nirdvaṃdvaḥ sukhī śānto nirāmayaḥ
english: Having passed from the immortal to the immortal, grown cool, freed of self-clinging, become Brahman, beyond all pairs of opposites — he is happy, at peace, and untouched by ill.

sanskrit: brahmasthānam anāvartam ekam akṣarasaṃjñakam aduḥkham ajaraṃ śāntaṃ sthānaṃ tat pratipadyate
english: He attains that abode of Brahman from which there is no returning, the One named the Imperishable — that station free from sorrow, free from age, and serene.

sanskrit: caturbhir lakṣaṇair hīnaṃ tathā ṣaḍbhiḥ saṣoḍaśaiḥ puruṣaṃ samatikramya ākāśaṃ pratipadyate
english: Transcending the Puruṣa that is marked off by four signs, by six, and by sixteen, he attains the ether-like Absolute.

sanskrit: atha vecchati rāgātmā sarvaṃ tad adhitiṣṭhati yac ca prārthayate tac ca manasā pratipadyate
english: But if, his nature still passionate, he desires, he presides over all that; and whatever he prays for, that he attains by the mind alone.

sanskrit: atha vā vīkṣate lokān sarvān nirayasaṃsthitān niḥspṛhaḥ sarvato muktas tatraiva ramate sukhī
english: Or else, free of craving and released from all things, he looks upon all the worlds set forth before him as in a hall, and rejoices there in happiness.

sanskrit: evam eṣā mahārāja jāpakasya gatir yathā etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Such, great king, is the course of the reciter. All this I have declared to you. What further do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kim uttaraṃ tadā tau sma cakratus tena bhāṣite brāhmaṇo vātha vā rājā tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When that had been spoken, what answer did the two then make — the brāhmaṇa, or else the king? Tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: atha vā tau gatau tatra yad etat kīrtitaṃ tvayā saṃvādo vā tayoḥ ko 'bhūt kiṃ vā tau tatra cakratuḥ
english: Or did the two then depart to that place of which you have spoken? What dialogue passed between them, and what did they do there?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tathety evaṃ pratiśrutya dharmaṃ saṃpūjya cābhibho yamaṃ kālaṃ ca mṛtyuṃ ca svargaṃ saṃpūjya cārhataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having assented, saying "So be it," and having honored Dharma, O lord, and reverenced the worthy ones — Yama, Time, Death, and Heaven —

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ ye cāpare tatra sametā brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ sarvān saṃpūjya śirasā rājānaṃ so 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: and having bowed his head to all the bulls among brāhmaṇas, those of old and the others assembled there, the brāhmaṇa spoke these words to the king:

sanskrit: phalenānena saṃyukto rājarṣe gaccha puṇyatām bhavatā cābhyanujñāto japeyaṃ bhūya eva hi
english: "Endowed with this fruit, O royal sage, go to your holy reward; and with your leave I would recite once more."

sanskrit: varaś ca mama pūrvaṃ hi devyā datto mahābala śraddhā te japato nityaṃ bhaviteti viśāṃ pate
english: "For long ago, O mighty one, the goddess granted me a boon, O lord of peoples: 'Faith shall be ever yours as you recite.'"

sanskrit: rājovāca yady evam aphalā siddhiḥ śraddhā ca japituṃ tava gaccha vipra mayā sārdhaṃ jāpakaṃ phalam āpnuhi
english: The king said: "If thus your perfection bears no fruit, yet you have faith to recite, then come, brāhmaṇa, along with me, and obtain the reciter's reward."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca kṛtaḥ prayatnaḥ sumahān sarveṣāṃ saṃnidhāv iha saha tulyaphalau cāvāṃ gacchāvo yatra nau gatiḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "A very great effort has been made here in the presence of all. Equal in fruit, let us two go together to wherever our course leads."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vyavasāyaṃ tayos tatra viditvā tridaśeśvaraḥ saha devair upayayau lokapālais tathaiva ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Knowing the resolve of the two, the lord of the thirty gods drew near, together with the gods and likewise with the guardians of the worlds.

sanskrit: sādhyā viśve 'tha maruto jyotīṃṣi sumahānti ca nadyaḥ śailāḥ samudrāś ca tīrthāni vividhāni ca
english: The Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the Maruts, and the mighty luminaries, the rivers, mountains, and oceans, and the many places of pilgrimage —

sanskrit: tapāṃsi saṃyogavidhir vedāḥ stobhāḥ sarasvatī nāradaḥ parvataś caiva viśvāvasur hahā huhūḥ
english: the austerities, the rule of ritual conjunction, the Vedas, the chanted syllables, Sarasvatī, Nārada, and Parvata, Viśvāvasu, Hāhā and Hūhū —

sanskrit: gandharvaś citrasenaś ca parivāragaṇair yutaḥ nāgāḥ siddhāś ca munayo devadevaḥ prajāpatiḥ viṣṇuḥ sahasraśīrṣaś ca devo 'cintyaḥ samāgamat
english: the gandharva Citrasena with his retinue of attendants, the nāgas, the siddhas, and the sages; the God of gods, Prajāpati; and Viṣṇu the thousand-headed, the inconceivable deity — all came together.

sanskrit: avādyantāntarikṣe ca bheryas tūryāṇi cābhibho puṣpavarṣāṇi divyāni tatra teṣāṃ mahātmanām nanṛtuś cāpsaraḥsaṃghās tatra tatra samantataḥ
english: In the midspace, O lord, kettledrums and trumpets sounded; divine showers of blossoms fell upon those great souls, and troops of apsarases danced everywhere on every side.

sanskrit: atha svargas tathā rūpī brāhmaṇaṃ vākyam abravīt saṃsiddhas tvaṃ mahābhāga tvaṃ ca siddhas tathā nṛpa
english: Then Heaven himself, in visible form, spoke these words to the brāhmaṇa: "You are perfected, O blessed one; and you too are perfected, O king."

sanskrit: atha tau sahitau rājann anyonyena vidhānataḥ viṣayapratisaṃhāram ubhāv eva pracakratuḥ
english: Then, O king, the two together, each in due order, both performed the withdrawal of the senses from their objects.

sanskrit: prāṇāpānau tathodānaṃ samānaṃ vyānam eva ca evaṃ tān manasi sthāpya dadhatuḥ prāṇayor manaḥ
english: Prāṇa and apāna, udāna, samāna, and vyāna — having fixed these breaths in the mind, they then placed the mind upon the vital breaths.

sanskrit: upasthitakṛtau tatra nāsikāgram adho bhruvau kuṅkuṇyāṃ caiva manasā śanair dhārayataḥ sma tau
english: Steady in their posture there, the two slowly held the mind, with eyes upon the tip of the nose, below the brows, fixed upon the seat within.

sanskrit: niśceṣṭābhyāṃ śarīrābhyāṃ sthiradṛṣṭī samāhitau jitāsanau tathādhāya mūrdhany ātmānam eva ca
english: With bodies wholly motionless, gaze unwavering, deep in concentration, masters of their seat, they fixed the very self within the crown of the head.

sanskrit: tāludeśam athoddālya brāhmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ jyotirjvālā sumahatī jagāma tridivaṃ tadā
english: Then, bursting through the region of the palate of the great-souled brāhmaṇa, a vast flame of light went up to the third heaven.

sanskrit: hāhākāras tato dikṣu sarvāsu sumahān abhūt taj jyotiḥ stūyamānaṃ sma brahmāṇaṃ prāviśat tadā
english: Then a great cry of wonder arose in all the quarters; and that light, hymned with praise, entered then into Brahmā.

sanskrit: tataḥ svāgatam ity āha tat tejaḥ sa pitāmahaḥ prādeśamātraṃ puruṣaṃ pratyudgamya viśāṃ pate
english: Then the Grandfather, rising to meet that radiance — the Puruṣa no larger than a span — said "Welcome," O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: bhūyaś caivāparaṃ prāha vacanaṃ madhuraṃ sma saḥ jāpakais tulyaphalatā yogānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: And further he spoke another word, a sweet one: "The yogins have a fruit equal to that of the reciters — herein is no doubt."

sanskrit: yogasya tāvad etebhyaḥ phalaṃ pratyakṣadarśanam jāpakānāṃ viśiṣṭaṃ tu pratyutthānaṃ samādhikam
english: "For yoga the fruit, in comparison with these, is direct vision; but for the reciters the rising-up to meet them is a greater distinction still."

sanskrit: uṣyatāṃ mayi cety uktvācetayat sa tataḥ punaḥ athāsya praviveśāsyaṃ brāhmaṇo vigatajvaraḥ
english: Saying "Let him dwell in me," he then restored him to awareness once more; and the brāhmaṇa, his fever of passion gone, entered into His mouth.

sanskrit: rājāpy etena vidhinā bhagavantaṃ pitāmaham yathaiva dvijaśārdūlas tathaiva prāviśat tadā
english: The king too, by this same method, entered then into the blessed Grandfather, just as the tiger among brāhmaṇas had done.

sanskrit: svayaṃbhuvam atho devā abhivādya tato 'bruvan jāpakārtham ayaṃ yatnas tadarthaṃ vayam āgatāḥ
english: Then the gods, having saluted the Self-Existent, spoke: "This effort was for the reciter's sake, and for that we have come."

sanskrit: kṛtapūjāv imau tulyaṃ tvayā tulyaphalāv imau yogajāpakayor dṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ sumahad adya vai sarvāṃl lokān atītyaitau gacchetāṃ yatra vāñchitam
english: "These two have been honored alike by you, and alike in their fruit. The fruit of the yogin and of the reciter has this day been seen to be very great. Let these two pass beyond all the worlds and go wherever they wish."

sanskrit: brahmovāca mahāsmṛtiṃ paṭhed yas tu tathaivānusmṛtiṃ śubhām tāv apy etena vidhinā gacchetāṃ matsalokatām
english: Brahmā said: "Whoever recites the Mahāsmṛti, and likewise the auspicious Anusmṛti — those two also, by this method, would attain to a shared world with me."

sanskrit: yaś ca yoge bhaved bhaktaḥ so 'pi nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ vidhinānena dehānte mama lokān avāpnuyāt gamyatāṃ sādhayiṣyāmi yathāsthānāni siddhaye
english: "And whoever is devoted to yoga — he too, of this there is no doubt, would by this method attain my worlds at the body's end. Let it be so; I shall bring it about, that each may reach his proper station for perfection."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktvā sa tadā devas tatraivāntaradhīyata āmantrya taṃ tato devā yayuḥ svaṃ svaṃ niveśanam
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, the god then vanished on the spot; and the gods, taking their leave of him, departed each to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: te ca sarve mahātmāno dharmaṃ satkṛtya tatra vai pṛṣṭhato 'nuyayū rājan sarve suprītamānasāḥ
english: And all those great souls, having honored Dharma there, followed after, O king, all of them with hearts well pleased.

sanskrit: etat phalaṃ jāpakānāṃ gatiś caiva prakīrtitā yathāśrutaṃ mahārāja kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: This is the fruit of the reciters, and their course has been proclaimed, just as I have heard it, great king. What further do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ phalaṃ jñānayogasya vedānāṃ niyamasya ca bhūtātmā vā kathaṃ jñeyas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is the fruit of the yoga of knowledge, of the Vedas, and of self-restraint? And how is the Self of beings to be known? Tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam manoḥ prajāpater vādaṃ maharṣeś ca bṛhaspateḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite an ancient story — the discourse between Manu the Lord of creatures and the great sage Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: prajāpatiṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ pṛthivyāṃ; devarṣisaṃghapravaro maharṣiḥ bṛhaspatiḥ praśnam imaṃ purāṇaṃ; papraccha śiṣyo 'tha guruṃ praṇamya
english: Bṛhaspati, the great sage, foremost of the host of divine seers, bowing as a disciple to his teacher, asked this ancient question of Prajāpati, the most excellent upon the earth:

sanskrit: yatkāraṇaṃ mantravidhiḥ pravṛtto; jñāne phalaṃ yat pravadanti viprāḥ yan mantraśabdair akṛtaprakāśaṃ; tad ucyatāṃ me bhagavan yathāvat
english: "For what cause is the rite of sacred formulas set in motion? What fruit do the brāhmaṇas declare to lie in knowledge? And that which is not made manifest by the words of the formulas — let it be told to me truly, O blessed one."

sanskrit: yad arthaśāstrāgamamantravidbhir; yajñair anekair varagopradānaiḥ phalaṃ mahadbhir yad upāsyate ca; tat kiṃ kathaṃ vā bhavitā kva vā tat
english: "That great fruit which is sought by those versed in the treatises, the scriptures, and the formulas, through many sacrifices and gifts of choice cattle — what is it, and how, and where shall it come to be?"

sanskrit: mahī mahījāḥ pavano 'ntarikṣaṃ; jalaukasaś caiva jalaṃ divaṃ ca divaukasaś caiva yataḥ prasūtās; tad ucyatāṃ me bhagavan purāṇam
english: "The earth and earth-born things, the wind and the midspace, the water-dwellers and the water, the heaven and the heaven-dwellers — that ancient source from which they sprang, let it be told to me, O blessed one."

sanskrit: jñānaṃ yataḥ prārthayate naro vai; tatas tadarthā bhavati pravṛttiḥ na cāpy ahaṃ veda paraṃ purāṇaṃ; mithyāpravṛttiṃ ca kathaṃ nu kuryām
english: "Since a man longs for knowledge, his striving is directed to that end. Yet I do not know the supreme and ancient One — and how then should I undertake a striving that is false?"

sanskrit: ṛk sāmasaṃghāṃś ca yajūṃṣi cāhaṃ; chandāṃsi nakṣatragatiṃ niruktam adhītya ca vyākaraṇaṃ sakalpaṃ; śikṣāṃ ca bhūtaprakṛtiṃ na vedmi
english: "Though I have studied the Ṛc and the bodies of Sāman and the Yajus chants, the meters, the course of the constellations, etymology, grammar with the ritual codes, and phonetics — still I do not know the primordial nature of beings."

sanskrit: sa me bhavāñ śaṃsatu sarvam etaj; jñāne phalaṃ karmaṇi vā yad asti yathā ca dehāc cyavate śarīrī; punaḥ śarīraṃ ca yathābhyupaiti
english: "Let your honor declare to me all this: what fruit there is in knowledge or in action; and how the embodied one falls away from the body, and how it comes again to a body."

sanskrit: manur uvāca yad yat priyaṃ yasya sukhaṃ tad āhus; tad eva duḥkhaṃ pravadanty aniṣṭam iṣṭaṃ ca me syād itarac ca na syād; etatkṛte karmavidhiḥ pravṛttaḥ iṣṭaṃ tv aniṣṭaṃ ca na māṃ bhajetety; etatkṛte jñānavidhiḥ pravṛttaḥ
english: Manu said: Whatever is dear to a man they call his pleasure; that very same thing, when unwished-for, they call his pain. "May the wished-for be mine, and may the other not be" — for this the rule of action is set in motion. "May neither the wished-for nor the unwished-for come upon me" — for this the rule of knowledge is set in motion.

sanskrit: kāmātmakāś chandasi karmayogā; ebhir vimuktaḥ param aśnuvīta nānāvidhe karmapathe sukhārthī; naraḥ pravṛtto na paraṃ prayāti paraṃ hi tat karmapathād apetaṃ; nirāśiṣaṃ brahmaparaṃ hy avaśyam
english: The works of ritual action in the Vedas are rooted in desire; freed from these, a man may attain the Supreme. The man who, seeking happiness, has set out upon the manifold path of action does not reach the Supreme; for the Supreme stands apart from the path of action — free of all petition, given over wholly to Brahman.

sanskrit: prajāḥ sṛṣṭā manasā karmaṇā ca; dvāv apy etau satpathau lokajuṣṭau dṛṣṭvā karma śāśvataṃ cāntavac ca; manastyāgaḥ kāraṇaṃ nānyad asti
english: Creatures are brought forth by mind and by action; both these are good paths, frequented by the world. Seeing that action is everlasting yet also has an end, the renunciation of the mind is the cause of release — there is no other.

sanskrit: svenātmanā cakṣur iva praṇetā; niśātyaye tamasā saṃvṛtātmā jñānaṃ tu vijñānaguṇena yuktaṃ; karmāśubhaṃ paśyati varjanīyam
english: At the passing of night, the self enveloped in darkness is its own guide, as the eye is a guide; but knowledge, joined with the quality of discernment, sees that evil action is to be shunned.

sanskrit: sarpān kuśāgrāṇi tathodapānaṃ; jñātvā manuṣyāḥ parivarjayanti ajñānatas tatra patanti mūḍhā; jñāne phalaṃ paśya yathā viśiṣṭam
english: Knowing them for what they are, men avoid serpents, the sharp points of kuśa grass, and the open well; but the deluded, through ignorance, fall into them. See how distinguished is the fruit that lies in knowledge.

sanskrit: kṛtsnas tu mantro vidhivat prayukto; yajñā yathoktās tv atha dakṣiṇāś ca annapradānaṃ manasaḥ samādhiḥ; pañcātmakaṃ karmaphalaṃ vadanti
english: The whole formula duly employed, the sacrifices as prescribed, the priestly fees, the giving of food, and the concentration of the mind — fivefold, they say, is the fruit of action.

sanskrit: guṇātmakaṃ karma vadanti vedās; tasmān mantrā mantramūlaṃ hi karma vidhir vidheyaṃ manasopapattiḥ; phalasya bhoktā tu yathā śarīrī
english: The Vedas declare action to consist of the qualities; therefore the formulas, and the formula is the root of action; the rule is to be carried out, and its fulfillment is by the mind. But the enjoyer of the fruit is the embodied self.

sanskrit: śabdāś ca rūpāṇi rasāś ca puṇyāḥ; sparśāś ca gandhāś ca śubhās tathaiva naro nasaṃsthānagataḥ prabhuḥ syād; etat phalaṃ sidhyati karmaloke
english: Sounds and forms and pleasant tastes, touches and fragrances likewise auspicious — and a man may become a lord, dwelling among them: this is the fruit that is won in the world of action.

sanskrit: yad yac charīreṇa karoti karma; śarīrayuktaḥ samupāśnute tat śarīram evāyatanaṃ sukhasya; duḥkhasya cāpy āyatanaṃ śarīram
english: Whatever action one does with the body, being joined to a body one enjoys it; the body is the very seat of pleasure, and the body is the seat of pain as well.

sanskrit: vācā tu yat karma karoti kiṃ cid; vācaiva sarvaṃ samupāśnute tat manas tu yat karma karoti kiṃ cin; manaḥstha evāyam upāśnute tat
english: Whatever action one does by speech, by speech one fully enjoys it all; and whatever action one does by the mind, abiding in the mind one enjoys that.

sanskrit: yathāguṇaṃ karmagaṇaṃ phalārthī; karoty ayaṃ karmaphale niviṣṭaḥ tathā tathāyaṃ guṇasaṃprayuktaḥ; śubhāśubhaṃ karmaphalaṃ bhunakti
english: As, seeking fruit, this self performs its host of deeds according to the qualities, intent upon the fruit of action, so, conjoined with those very qualities, it enjoys the good and evil fruit of action.

sanskrit: matsyo yathā srota ivābhipātī; tathā kṛtaṃ pūrvam upaiti karma śubhe tv asau tuṣyati duṣkṛte tu; na tuṣyate vai paramaḥ śarīrī
english: As a fish darts along, following the current, so one comes upon the action one did before. In the good deed the embodied one is content, but in the ill-done deed the supreme embodied one finds no content.

sanskrit: yato jagat sarvam idaṃ prasūtaṃ; jñātvātmavanto vyatiyānti yat tat yan mantraśabdair akṛtaprakāśaṃ; tad ucyamānaṃ śṛṇu me paraṃ yat
english: That from which this whole world is brought forth, which the masters of self come to know and pass beyond, that which is not made manifest by the words of the formulas — hear from me as I tell it, the Supreme:

sanskrit: rasair viyuktaṃ vividhaiś ca gandhair; aśabdam asparśam arūpavac ca agrāhyam avyaktam avarṇam ekaṃ; pañcaprakāraṃ sasṛje prajānām
english: Devoid of tastes and of the various fragrances, soundless, touchless, and without form, ungraspable, unmanifest, colorless, One — it brought forth the fivefold creation of beings.

sanskrit: na strī pumān vāpi napuṃsakaṃ ca; na san na cāsat sad asac ca tan na paśyanti yad brahmavido manuṣyās; tad akṣaraṃ na kṣaratīti viddhi
english: It is neither woman, nor man, nor neuter; neither being nor non-being, nor yet both being and non-being. That which the men who know Brahman behold — know it to be the Imperishable, for it does not perish.

sanskrit: manur uvāca akṣarāt khaṃ tato vāyur vāyor jyotis tato jalam jalāt prasūtā jagatī jagatyāṃ jāyate jagat
english: Manu said: From the Imperishable comes ether, from ether wind, from wind fire, and from fire water; from water the earth is brought forth, and upon the earth the world is born.

sanskrit: ime śarīrair jalam eva gatvā; jalāc ca tejaḥ pavano 'ntarikṣam khād vai nivartanti nabhāvinas te; ye bhāvinas te param āpnuvanti
english: These, with their bodies, pass into water, and from water into fire, into wind, into the midspace; those not destined for the Supreme turn back from the ether, but those who are destined attain the Supreme.

sanskrit: noṣṇaṃ na śītaṃ mṛdu nāpi tīkṣṇaṃ; nāmlaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ na tiktam na śabdavan nāpi ca gandhavat tan; na rūpavat tat paramasvabhāvam
english: Neither hot nor cold, neither soft nor sharp, neither sour, astringent, sweet, nor bitter; neither possessed of sound nor of fragrance, nor of form — such is That, the supreme essence.

sanskrit: sparśaṃ tanur veda rasaṃ tu jihvā; ghrāṇaṃ ca gandhāñ śravaṇe ca śabdān rūpāṇi cakṣur na ca tatparaṃ yad; gṛhṇanty anadhyātmavido manuṣyāḥ
english: The body knows touch, the tongue taste, the nose fragrances, the ears sounds, the eye forms; but that which is supreme beyond these — the men who do not know the inner Self cannot grasp it.

sanskrit: nivartayitvā rasanaṃ rasebhyo; ghrāṇaṃ ca gandhāc chravaṇe ca śabdāt sparśāt tanuṃ rūpaguṇāt tu cakṣus; tataḥ paraṃ paśyati svaṃ svabhāvam
english: Having drawn back the tongue from tastes, the nose from fragrance, the ears from sound, the body from touch, and the eye from the quality of form — beyond that he beholds his own essence.

sanskrit: yato gṛhītvā hi karoti yac ca; yasmiṃś ca tām ārabhate pravṛttim yasmiṃś ca yad yena ca yaś ca kartā; tatkāraṇaṃ taṃ samupāyam āhuḥ
english: That from which one takes hold and acts, and that in which one begins one's activity; that in which, that which, that by which, and the one who is the doer — that they call the cause and the means.

sanskrit: yac cābhibhūḥ sādhakaṃ vyāpakaṃ ca; yan mantravac chaṃsyate caiva loke yaḥ sarvahetuḥ paramārthakārī; tat kāraṇaṃ kāryam ato yad anyat
english: That which is sovereign, effecting and all-pervading, which is hymned in the world as in the formulas; He who is the cause of all and works the highest end — that is the Cause; whatever is other than it is effect.

sanskrit: yathā ca kaś cit sukṛtair manuṣyaḥ; śubhāśubhaṃ prāpnute 'thāvirodhāt evaṃ śarīreṣu śubhāśubheṣu; svakarmajair jñānam idaṃ nibaddham
english: As a man, by his good deeds, attains the good and the ill without conflict, so within bodies good and ill this knowledge is bound fast, born of one's own deeds.

sanskrit: yathā pradīpaḥ purataḥ pradīptaḥ; prakāśam anyasya karoti dīpyan tatheha pañcendriyadīpavṛkṣā; jñānapradīptāḥ paravanta eva
english: As a lamp kindled before one, blazing, gives light to another, so here the five senses, lamp-trees set ablaze by knowledge, are yet dependent on another.

sanskrit: yathā hi rājño bahavo hy amātyāḥ; pṛthak pramānaṃ pravadanti yuktāḥ tadvac charīreṣu bhavanti pañca; jñānaikadeśaḥ paramaḥ sa tebhyaḥ
english: For just as the many ministers of a king, each in his appointed office, pronounce their judgment separately, so within bodies are the five senses; but the supreme one, the single seat of knowledge, stands above them all.
